entry.dc:title: Mud, mines and rainforest: A short history of human impact in western Tasmania, using pollen, trace metals and lead-210
entry.dc:creator: Harle K.
entry.dc:description: Lead-210, pollen and trace-element analyses of a finely sampled 7.5-cm sediment core from a subalpine tarn in western Tasmania have provided a detailed record of post-colonial human impact in the region. Lead-210 analysis indicated that the record extends back to about 1811 AD, with several changes in sediment rates evident. These have been tentatively related to disturbance in the catchment associated with ore prospecting. The regional vegetation has been reconstructed for this period using pollen abundances. Prior to 1860 AD, there appears to have been little disturbance in the regional vegetation, with relatively high taxon diversity and pollen concentrations. Important communities included rainforest dominated by Nothofagus cunninghamii and subdominated by Phyllocladus and Eucryphia, eucalypt-dominated mixed and wet sclerophyll forest and subalpine and/or alpine complexes. From the 1860s, the evidence suggests an overall reduction in the extent of regional forests, particularly rainforest and subalpine woodland. Initially, this appears to have been associated with both elevated charcoal levels and minor increases in concentrations of trace metals, particularly lead, tin, arsenic and copper. By the 1950s, however, significant reductions in taxon diversity and pollen abundance (particularly for rainforest and subalpine woodland) were strongly associated with rapidly increasing concentrations of trace metals. This evidence corresponds with historic records of mineral prospecting and mining in the region, especially around Queenstown where significant deforestation occurred due to logging and pollution from smelters. Interestingly, the evidence for the most significant impacts coincided with the escalation of open-cut mining from the 1950s to the 1970s, rather than earlier phases of smelter-produced pollution.

entry.dc:title: Heroic Failure? Unionism and Queensland's Coal Communities, 1954–67
entry.dc:creator: Bowden B.
entry.dc:description: This article records the struggle waged by the Queensland Colliery Employees ‘Union, the state branch of the Miners’ Federation, in defence of jobs between 1954 and 1967. This struggle was unsuccessful, in that it failed to achieve its objective of protecting underground jobs. Despite this failure, however, the campaign to defend the collieries managed to overcome the traditionally locality-based outlook of Queensland's coal miners, producing organising techniques and an industrial vision that proved the salvation of the union. When the union began a large-scale organising campaign in open-cut mining after 1967 it took to this new sector a tradition of militancy and resistance that no other coal union could equal.

entry.dc:title: The avifauna of the forests of south-west Western Australia: Changes in species composition, distribution, and abundance following anthropogenic disturbance
entry.dc:creator: Abbott I.
entry.dc:description: The avifauna (land and waterbirds) of the forests of southwest Western Australia is circumscribed by reference to information recorded in the period 1840 to 1998. A database was assembled from 272 published and unpublished bird lists, and this was supplemented with records extracted from a systematic search of the primary ornithological literature. In excess of 7 000 records were located. The original forest avifauna (just before the impact of European settlers became pronounced) consisted of 112 breeding species (81 land, 31 water). Salient characteristics of this avifauna include: only 1 species is confined (as a breeding species) to the primaeval forest ecosystem; 53 species occur throughout the forests; 32 and 13 species are restricted to its eastern or southern portions respectively; most species occur extensively outside of the forests (66 species to the west, north, east and south; 33 species to the west, north and east); 52 per cent of landbird species are insectivores; about 20 per cent of the landbird fauna migrates from the forest in varying degrees in winter; 67 per cent of landbird species nest in the overstorey or understorey; and landbirds in streamside forests occur at higher densities than in upland forests. The distribution of 5 species - Leipoa ocellata (Malleefowl), Cacatua pastinator (Western long-billed corella), Atrichornis clamosus (Noisy scrub-bird), Falcunculus frontatus (Crested shrike-tit) and Rallus pectoralis (Lewin's rail) - is discussed in detail, with new or neglected information being provided. The landbird fauna of the primaeval forest is impoverished relative to elsewhere in the South West Land Division, particularly the region now known as the wheatbelt. The forests of south-west Western Australia have only about half of the number of bird species present in a similar-sized, comparable area in south-east Australia. The south-west forest avifauna is more similar to that present in the Mount Lofty Ranges (South Australia) than to the forest avifaunas of New South Wales or Tasmania. At local scales (1-100 ha), however, the number of landbird species present is similar in all forests in southern mainland Australia (20-25 breeding species). Overall density of bird populations in jarrah and karri forests is about one half of that in comparable forests in south-east Australia. Disturbances caused by European settlement have resulted in 4 species present in the primal forests contracting in geographical range, 2 species becoming extinct, and more than 90 species benefiting from provision of new habitats. Forest management has had limited impact on biodiversity and total abundance of birds. Prescribed burning under moist soil conditions has no impact on bird species richness in jarrah forest, but increases bird species richness in karri forest for 3-6 years. Total abundance of birds increases in both types of forest after prescribed burning. Planned burning under dry soil conditions increases both bird species richness and total abundance of birds. Wildfire reduces bird species richness. All of these changes are temporary. Thinning of jarrah forest does not change bird species richness, whereas cutting to gaps increases bird species richness. Clearfelling of karri forest initially reduces bird species richness; 12 years later about 85 per cent of the avifauna in mature stands is present in regrowth karri forest. Those species dependent on large hollows for nesting are unlikely to nest in unthinned regrowth forest younger than about 120 years. Open-cut mining for bauxite has a severe initial impact on bird species richness, but following rehabilitation there is a rapid return of bird species, with 85 per cent of species present before mining being recorded after 5 years. Species requiring large hollows for nesting cannot, however, nest in rehabilitated sites for many decades. The most severe, long term reduction in local bird species richness and total abundance is caused by dieback disease and by permanent removal of forest as in agriculture, urbanization, damming of rivers, and plantations of pine. However, an additional 75 species (51 land, 24 water) have been recorded within the forests following clearing for farming and towns. Of these species, 23 (17 land, 6 water) now breed, but only two of them (Aquila morphnoides Little eagle, Dacelo novaeguineae Laughing kookaburra) breed in forest. The policies and procedures in place to mitigate the impact of humans on the forest bird fauna and to promote the conservation of bird species are summarized. These include an extensive mosaic of protected areas (national parks, nature reserves, forest along roads, rivers and streams), a structural goal of 40 per cent of the forest being maintained at the mature or senescent stage, the retention of habitat trees for species dependent on hollows for nesting, and spatially and temporally diversified use of fire.

entry.dc:title: Simulation of GPS performance in open cut mines
entry.dc:creator: Walker R.
entry.dc:description: Many problems exist for high performance users of GPS in the open-cut mining environment. The basic requirements are that a suitable number of multipath free signals are available and, if the system is to be used in real-time, the continuous availability of a high performance communications link. These two basic criteria are not readily fulfilled in the mining environment, where the rugged shape of the terrain can severely limit the availability of a communications link due to high shadow losses which can also imply significant multipath reflections of the GPS signal.

entry.dc:title: Soil cover of the ket-kap mountain massif and its transformation under the influence of open-cut mining
entry.dc:creator: Gyninova A.
entry.dc:description: Industrial gold mining in the north of the Khabarovskii region results in deterioration of natural landscapes in valleys of mountain rivers. Restoration of soil cover is hampered by degradation of permafrost and soil-forming rocks. It is recommended that the influence of the components of natural and technogenic landscapes should be taken into account in the process of soil reclamation. entry.dc:title: Preventive maintenance of open-cut continuous mining equipment
entry.dc:creator: Feder D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Welding in the World Le Soudage Dans Le Monde
entry.dc:description: Lignite mined in open cuts is a very economical source of fossil fuel, especially when continuous mining equipment is employed. Development of design rules and typical fatigue loads for the structures of open-cut mining machines are discussed. In view of the limited accuracy of fatigue strength prediction and stress analysis, economical design and safe operation require regular in-service inspections for fatigue cracks. The practice that has been established for these inspections is described. In concluding, some reasons for fatigue failures observed over the years are reported.

entry.dc:title: Approximations for heterogeneous finite source queues
entry.dc:creator: Carmichael D.
entry.dc:description: The exact solution for heterogeneous finite source queues involves a definition of state which is unmanageable for large customer numbers. Accordingly various approximations are considered in an attempt to obtain a simple but reasonably accurate solution. The approximations examine simplified definitions of state with a consequent reduction in the number of states and associated balance equations: one such approximation converts the heterogeneous problem to an equivalent homogeneous problem through either time- or rate-averaging the problem components. Applications include earthmoving, quarrying and open-cut mining operations where the plant frequently have different characteristics. The exponential solution in such cases is anticipated to provide a ower bound estimate on operation productivity, by analogy with the homogeneous case. © 1991, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: VLF surface impedance mapping of coal seams
entry.dc:creator: Thiel D.V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Digest International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium IGARSS
entry.dc:description: Summary form only given, as follows. On the north eastern coast of Australia are found some of the largest continuous coal seams on the world. The relative uniformity of these seams in both depth to coal and depth of coal provide an ideal environment to assess the potential of coal seam mapping using surface impedance measurements. The purpose of such measurements is to reduce the number of exploratory drill holes required prior to open-cut mining, but still to retain the integrity of the information supplied to mine planners. Since 1986, a number of detailed VLF surface impedance surveys were conducted at a number of coal fields. A problem of concern to coal mine planners is the continuity of the coal seam in the next blocks to be mined. Case studies included the detection of hard rock instructions, conductive dykes, and significant faulting structures in the coal. Results have been checked by drilling and evidence in the high wall of mined out blocks. These types of dislocations offer important information about the fundamental nature of the interaction of plane polarized horizontal electromagnetic waves with a variety of different structures. Surface impedance measurements were made using an in-house VLF receiver system and insulated antenna field probe. The somewhat different design is thought to have many advantages over more traditional techniques. These advantages include the lateral resolution achievable, the speed of measurement and so of traverse, and the immediate presentation of data in the field.

entry.dc:title: Use of the standardized ESSY grease lubricating system for open-cut mining equipment
entry.dc:creator: Neumann K.
entry.dc:description: A lubricating system enabling numerous lube points to be supplied with lubricants over great distances and under extremely difficult operating conditions is described. The system improves equipment reliability, assures long equipment life, and provides for a low level of equipment maintenance. (English abstract)

entry.dc:title: Queue simulation of cyclic construction operations
entry.dc:creator: Carmichael D.
entry.dc:description: Cyclic construction operations may be modelled in terms of the waiting times of the entities (typically equipment, plant, materials or manpower) that repeatedly pass through the various phases of the cycle. The relevant model involves recursive expressions linking the waiting times of successive cycles. This permits a Monte Carlo type simulation to be carried out and represents an alternative method to conventional event or time-oriented simulation and queueing theory. The elementary form of the recursive expressions for the waiting times results in a short computer program and minimal computer demands, enabling the simulation to be carried out on the smallest of microcomputers. The paper develops the simulation approach and makes a comparison with queueing theory. Both random sampling and a variance reduction technique are used. Models are developed for earthmoving, quarrying and open-cut mining applications in elementary cycle form and multiple phase form. ftI9XX. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Recultivation of the spoil banks created by open-cut mining activities in Hungary
entry.dc:creator: Szegi J.
entry.dc:description: Recultivation processes in the area of the Visonta open-cut mine enterprise were studied. Different recultivation efforts have been combined to form a landscape protection plan, which is responsible for preservation and enhancement of landscape potential. The recolonization of microorganisms and natural vegetation were studied during the different phases of recultivation. A special soil-estimation system was developed to determine the economical usefulness of recultivated spoils. Basic principles for a combined recultivation process were introduced.

entry.dc:title: Optimal shovel-truck operations
entry.dc:creator: Carmichael D.
entry.dc:description: Charts are presented as the solution of the optimal shovel-truck configuration problem. In particular, for given parameters defining the shovel-truck operation (namely average haul, load and manoeuvre times), the charts enable the determination of the optimal truck fleet size. The objective function is one of cost per unit production of the operation. The model of the operation is based on finite source queueing theory results. Several queueing models are outlined and the sensitivity of the optimum solution to the assumed model is examined. Time and production constraints may be included with little extra work. The charts provide an effective and quick means for establishing the optimum truck fleet size in any earthmoving, quarrying or open-cut mining operation of the shovel-truck type. © 1986, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: LIGNITE MINING IN THE GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC (GDR) - PROBLEMS OF EFFECTIVE EXPLORATION AND EXTRACTION.
entry.dc:creator: Strzodka K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The GDR has extensive lignite deposits and beyond 2000, lignite will remain the most important source of primary energy in the national economy. The lignite is extracted by open-cut mining. In the future, the technology will be further developed in order to be able to extract low lying seams deposited in depth of up to 200 m.

entry.dc:title: Analysis of mineral wear processes with particular reference to open-cut mining equipment.
entry.dc:creator: Besser D.
entry.dc:description: Abrasive wear process are marked by high intensities of wear. Such wearing processes can be classified in three large groups, the most complex group being that of 3-body wear in which two solid bodies are moving against each other under the influence of mineral abrasives. Influential factors affecting such processes were analyzed in the laboratory, and the results obtained were confirmed by those obtained for lignite opencast mining equipment. (English abstract)

entry.dc:title: Accuracy of terrestrial stereophotogrammetric survey of quarries.
entry.dc:creator: Bruevic P.
entry.dc:description: A methodology is explained for calculating the accuracy of terrestrial photogrammetric survey of quarry benching in relation to the photogrammetric intersection angle at the observed point. It is proved that in the equally-deflected case of survey the accuracy of the results decreases toward the edges of the stereopair to be processed. A new practical approach is recommended for the pre-calculation of the parameters of terrestrial photogrammetric survey of open-cut mining places. -ITC Bibliography

entry.dc:title: ( Aerophotogrammetric precision survey of point shifts in browncoal open-cut mining areas).
entry.dc:creator: Reichenbach K.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Archives of Photogrammetry Vol 23 Part B4 Commission IV
entry.dc:description: Horizontal and vertical soil movements may occur at the edge of big open-cut mines. Terrestrial measurements for recording horizontal movements are so costly that aerophotogrammetry may be an economical alternative. A test programme is described for establishing the accuracy of point shift measurements in groups of photographs combined in many ways from quadruple flights. The accuracies attained with the Zeiss Planimat, Planicomp and PSK from wide-angle photographs at a photo scale of 1:7000 and various, also self-calibrating block adjustment programmes are compared with terrestrial control measurements. -from ITC Bibliography

entry.dc:title: Air photography and questions relating to an operative planning and control of open-cut mining operations.
entry.dc:creator: Zabrodin G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Metodika I Technika Markseyderskich Rabot Leningrad
entry.dc:description: The main characteristics of the open-cut mining method for mineral resources are discussed from the point of view of operative production control. The demands made on derived drawings of graphic mining documentation are quoted. The part of air photography in the mining-geodetic attendance of open-cut mining operations is shown. A new type of documentation is made on its basis - the negative map, considerably surpassing the mining-geodetic pit map by its clearness and information content. -from ITC Bibliography

entry.dc:title: Analytical aerial triangulation - a new method for constructing mine surveying networks in open-cut mining.
entry.dc:creator: Finarevsky I.
entry.prism:publicationName: Markseyderskoe Delo V Socialisti Ceskich Stranach
entry.dc:description: In periodical air photography of open-cut mines, analytical aerial triangulation using a computer is recommended with photographic extension beyond the mines. The network includes survey control stations and additional points, required for forming a digital model of the quarry, according to which mine surveying maps are compiled and the extent of the mining operations is determined. The method is considered to be very effective. -ITC Bibliography

entry.dc:description: According to the findings of the cost/output analysis carried out by the author, hydraulic excavators of the large-capacity classes (approx. 3. 5 to 7. 5 m**3) offer the most economic solution for loading operations in open-cut mining and quarrying.

entry.dc:title: Rate of development of mining operations in open pits
entry.dc:creator: Molotilov S.G.
entry.dc:description: 1. In open-cut mining of flat-lying deposits in the Kuzbass there is much scope for increasing the rate of development of mining operations. 2. In open pits in the Kuzbass, the rate of advance of the front of operations can be increased by a factor of 2-3 by increasing the excavator bucket capacity to 8 m<sup>3</sup>, constructing additional exchange stations on the working benches, increasing the load capacity of the trains to 800-900 tons, reducing the bench height to 15 m, and increasing the number of excavators per transport outlet to two when the length of the front of operations is 2.0 km or more. Realization of these suggestions could reduce the costs of mining operations by 11%. 3. The sinking rate of pits in deposits with flat-lying seams can be increased by a factor of 2-3 by using the scheme suggested in this article for cutting the open-cut trenches in layers with the upper layer of the trench leading the lower by the width of the working area, by increasing the excavator bucket capacity to 10-12 m<sup>3</sup>, by constructing an independent transport outlet on the intermediate horizon, by increasing the load capacity of the trains to 800-900 tons, by constructing additional exchange stations on the transport horizons, and by increasing the number of excavators on each layer of the trench to two when the length of the front of operations is 2.0 km or more. Realization of these suggestions could reduce the costs of cutting the open-cut trench by 20%. 4. Establishment of a course for increasing the rate of mining operations, which in further investigations will be linked with the load capacity of the transport communications of the pits, in comparison with other types of transport, enables us to devise a general strategy of technical policy for railroad transportation. © 1977 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
